cohort: The study included 100 women diagnosed with ectopic pregnancy identified from a total of 7685 births at a medical college during the same year.
finding: LSCS was identified as the predominant risk factor for ectopic pregnancy, accounting for 26% of cases, and 75% of patients undergoing surgery presented with ruptured ectopic pregnancies, limiting conservative treatment options.
mod_finding: Cesarean section (CS/LSCS) was identified as a predominant risk factor for ectopic pregnancy.
